text:
alice_support: :rotating_light: FYI customer reported a regression after today's canary -> prod migration. They say outputs are returning an old product template (OldWidget) instead of the new one (NewWidgetPro). Repro steps and snippets below.

alice_support: Request they hit: POST /v1/generate with body {
  "prompt": "PRODUCT_DESC: user=1234"
}

alice_support: Response (now):
```
{
  "text": "Our OldWidget is great for..."
}
```

alice_support: Response (pre-rollout / expected):
```
{
  "text": "NewWidgetPro delivers improved..."
}
```

alice_support: They said adding a request header x-disable-cache=1 made the response correct. No other code changes on their side.

jamie_runtime: thx. sounds like a KV/prefix cache hit with stale prefix mapping. can you include the model name and route? any chance they hit a routed model variant?

alice_support: route: prod/us-west/model-2.1, model name: rdlw/model-2.1-quant. customer says they hit it consistently after 11:05UTC when canary promoted.

jamie_runtime: can you try reproducing from our side and also call with header `x-disable-cache: 1` and `x-cache-bypass: true`? we need to confirm cache eviction behavior.

alice_support: repro from support workspace: with normal headers -> stale. with `x-disable-cache:1` -> returns NewWidgetPro.

noah_sre: posting infra note — deploy-bot shows the canary was promoted at 11:06 and the rollout included a cache key normalization tweak (PR #7123). possible mismatch between old cached prefix keys and new canonicalized keys leading to wrong prefix -> old KV entry returned.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout finished: service=runtime-serve env=prod us-west version=2026.3.11-rc2 commit=3a7f9b PR=7123 cache_normalize_prefix=true

elaine_eng: I pushed the canonicalization change. The intent was to normalize whitespace and lower-case prefixes, but I didn't add a migration for existing prefix entries. likely scenario: old keys stayed in cache, new requests canonicalize and point to a different keyspace, but requests routed to variant that still reads old prefix mapping. weird interplay.

jamie_runtime: ok. quick mitigation: 1) tell ops to invalidate prefix namespace for prod/us-west or flush affected prefix hash; 2) provide customer a short-term header they can set to bypass cache; 3) schedule hotfix that either backfills normalized keys or adds compatibility layer.

noah_sre: I can run a scoped flush for prefix namespace `prefix:PRODUCT_DESC` in prod/us-west. Will do if we confirm list of affected prefixes. ETA 7m.

alice_support: customer is on standby to test. requesting the flush now.

noah_sre: flush executed for namespace `prefix:PRODUCT_DESC` on prod/us-west at 11:18 UTC. logs: `flush_prefix(namespace=prefix:PRODUCT_DESC, scope=prod/us-west) -> ok`

alice_support: customer confirmed after flush: response now returns NewWidgetPro. they reverted to green. :tada:

elaine_eng: follow-up action items: 1) backfill normalized keys for the last 48h window (script ready), 2) add migration step to rollout tooling so canonicalization changes trigger prefix reconciliation, 3) add an automatic cache-compatibility test in the canary checklist. I'll open PRs.

maya_product: please prepare a short note to the customer explaining root cause (cache key normalization + missing migration) and actions taken. emphasize no user data exposed and we restored correct behavior.

jamie_runtime: also add a runtime probe that compares responses with and without cache-bypass during canary for a small % of traffic — will catch these regressions earlier.

alice_support: closing loop with customer now and will attach repro snippets + support logs. assigning follow-ups to @elaine_eng and @jamie_runtime. thanks all.

alice_support: summary: regression caused by prefix canonicalization change in PR#7123 leading to stale KV reads post-rollout. mitigated by flushing affected prefix namespace and planning backfill + migration in rollout flow.
